value.string: script_id, allow_empty=False, allow_overwrite_core=False, body=None, body_file=None, live_test=False, params=\'\', skin_folder=\'custom\', title=\'\'

Create or update a Python Script in portal_skins.
 
 ⚠ DESTRUCTIVE: deploys server-side code to ERP5. Writing a script with
 the same id as a framework script (e.g. Base_edit) shadows site-wide
 behavior. Overwriting an existing script replaces its body irreversibly.
 A short list of well-known framework script ids is guarded — pass
 allow_overwrite_core=True to bypass.
 
 Body guard: updating an EXISTING script requires an explicit body (or
 body_file) — a call with only script_id/skin_folder is refused with
 "body required to update an existing script (use erp5_skin_call to
 execute)" instead of silently emptying the script (session issue B6).
 An explicitly empty body ("") is refused too unless allow_empty=true.
 
 Creates the script if it doesn't exist, then updates it with the given
 body, params, and title. Uses the Zope Management Interface API.
 
 USE THIS WHEN:
 - You need to create a new Python Script in portal_skins (use 'body').
 - You want to update an existing Python Script's code, params, or title.
 - You're prototyping ERP5 business logic directly on an instance.
 
 Built-in feedback: the response echoes the params actually written, says
 whether the script is callable standalone (callable_standalone is false
 when it has a required/no-default param), and on a body that will not
 compile reports the real Zope compile traceback under 'error' instead of
 the terse "has errors" message (e.g. a nested 'def'). Set live_test=True
 to immediately re-invoke the written script (write-then-verify) and get
 its result in live_test_output; a live-test failure does not abort the write.
 
 Returns JSON with: status ("created" or "updated"), script_id, skin_folder,
 params, callable_standalone, plus (as applicable) error / hint / warning /
 live_test_runs / live_test_output / live_test_error.
